note: Hardware capability profiles keyed by canonical manufacturer (see MFR_ALIASES in scripts/build-cameras.mjs). 'profile' is shown on map popups when the model isn't tagged (almost always). Sources: FCC ID filings, ISED REL, teardowns, vendor datasheets — see data/research/. Seed data; expanded from certification-database research.

Flock Safety.radios: LTE Cat 4 (Sierra RC7611, FCC N7NRC76B) + Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) + Bluetooth 4.2 LE (LiteOn WCBN3510A, FCC PPQ-WCBN3510A) + GNSS. Newer units reportedly add an UNLABELED radar module with no FCC ID. Raven audio sensor: ESP32 Wi-Fi/BLE (beaconing) + LTE fallback.
Flock Safety.radiosSummary: Full radio stack — LTE, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GNSS; active hotspot; sniff-capable hardware
Flock Safety.confidence: confirmed (teardowns + module FCC IDs). Flock's own FCC grantee (2BKG8) has zero filings; no ISED Radio Equipment List entries found for Flock (live query) — devices ride third-party module certs.
Flock Safety.notes: No Canadian police contracts; Canadian pins are likely HOA/private or mistagged.

Genetec.radios: SharpV: optional LTE Cat-4 module + multi-GNSS; no Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth. SharpZ3 in-car: NO radios at all (GNSS receive-only option; backhaul via the patrol vehicle's own network). Cloudrunner: LTE Cat-4 + GPS only (Verizon ODI-verified).
Genetec.radiosSummary: No Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on any model — least sniff-capable of the major vendors (cert-verified)
Genetec.confidence: confirmed [CERT]: FCC applicant search 'Genetec' returns zero applications; ISED REL search returns none — LTE rides pre-certified third-party modules; no-radio variants are Part 15B only
Genetec.notes: Canada's most-deployed ALPR vendor (Montreal). Canadian cloud hosting; no vendor-run cross-agency search network.

Axon.radios: Outpost (FCC X4GS06009, ISED 8803A-S06009): LTE 9 bands incl. FirstNet B14 + dual-band Wi-Fi + BLE — one cert for the whole unit. Fleet 3: Wi-Fi + BT in cameras/hub, 900MHz FHSS wireless mics, GNSS; LTE via separate Cradlepoint router. Lightpost: radios live in Ubicquia's streetlight hub (FCC grantee 2AECK); camera is an Axis Q1800-LE.
Axon.radiosSummary: Cellular, dual-band Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios onboard (Outpost — certified by FCC and ISED filings)
Axon.confidence: confirmed [CERT]: FCC X4GS06009 (granted 2025-12-10) + ISED 8803A-S06009 (approved 2026-01-29 — Outpost is certified for the Canadian market)
Axon.notes: Toronto and York Region platform (Fusus). Customer-set retention, no vendor limit. Outpost's ISED approval (Jan 2026) means Axon's fixed ALPR hardware is regulatory-ready for Canada.

RTX Corporation.radios: Tolling gantry sensors (transponder readers + plate cameras)
RTX Corporation.radiosSummary: 407 toll system hardware — reads transponders and plates for billing
RTX Corporation.notes: These are the 407's toll cameras, operator-tagged as MTO. Not police surveillance.

Axis Communications.radios: None — PoE/DC wired only (P1445-LE-3, Q1700-LE: FCC Part 15B unintentional radiators; no FCC ID exists by design)
Axis Communications.radiosSummary: No radios — wired PoE; certified as an unintentional radiator
Axis Communications.confidence: confirmed (Axis datasheets: approvals list only FCC 15B/ICES-003 class marks)
Axis Communications.formFactor: Fixed IP camera, ALPR via analytics software
Axis Communications.notes: General-purpose IP cameras running plate-reading analytics.

Neology.radios: neoForce: unconfirmed; legacy PIPS TS-500 offered optional Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and internal modem
Neology.radiosSummary: Radio loadout unconfirmed (legacy PIPS units offered optional Wi-Fi/BT/modem)
Neology.confidence: partial (legacy PIPS docs; neoForce datasheet not public)
Neology.notes: BC provincial program vendor; BC deletes non-hit reads at end of shift.

Motorola Solutions.radiosSummary: Cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios onboard (L6Q)
Motorola Solutions.notes: Vigilant/DRN parent — the commercial-collection outlier in the US.

Dahua.radios: None — Ethernet RJ-45 only (ITC415/ITC215 datasheets); PoE+/12VDC/24VAC; FCC Part 15B class marks, no FCC ID
Dahua.radiosSummary: No radios — wired PoE. But vendor datasheet claims recognition of driver and front-seat passenger features
Dahua.formFactor: Fixed bullet, vertical pole mount, built-in IR
Dahua.notes: PRC vendor; banned from US federal procurement (NDAA s.889), FCC equipment authorizations halted 2022; still sold in Canada. Datasheet: 'supports recognizing... features of driver and front-seat passenger.'

Verkada.radios: Current CB52-TE/CB62-TE: PoE only. Gen-1 CB61-TE: contains a DORMANT Wi-Fi radio — disabled by default, enable requires Verkada Support at org level. New Outdoor Remote camera (FCC 2AWUU68B66001, Jan 2026): BLE + LTE.
Verkada.radiosSummary: Current LPR bullets are wired PoE — but gen-1 units carry a dormant support-enabled Wi-Fi radio, and the newest remote camera ships BLE + LTE
Verkada.confidence: confirmed (datasheets + FCC grantee 2AWUU records + Verkada help docs)
Verkada.formFactor: Fixed bullet (telephoto/wide), LPR as cloud analytics
Verkada.notes: 2021 breach exposed ~150,000 customer camera feeds. Separate CR63-E 'remote' line has LTE.

Leonardo ELSAG.radios: Plate readers: wireless alarm broadcast (~0.5 mi); SignalTrace sensor adds Wi-Fi/BT/RF capture by design
Leonardo ELSAG.radiosSummary: Vendor of SignalTrace — device-signal capture as a product
Leonardo ELSAG.formFactor: In-car, fixed, covert pole/barrel, radar trailers
Leonardo ELSAG.notes: See the antenna problem — SignalTrace pairs device signals with plates.

Jenoptik.radios: VECTOR camera: no transmit radios (GPS receive-only, wired LAN). Paired 24 GHz enforcement radar is the certified transmitter (FCC grantee QJJ, e.g. QJJ-590113).
Jenoptik.radiosSummary: Camera itself transmit-silent; the radar beside it is the certified RF device. Vendor of TraffiCatch device-signal capture (separate product)
Jenoptik.formFactor: Fixed multi-lane (VECTOR/VECTOR2/3), average-speed P2P, trailer/portable; dual-sensor mono+colour
Jenoptik.notes: UK national ANPR mainstay; US border counties run VECTOR trailers with TraffiCatch — see the antenna problem.
